title: metadata-server exceeds_max_depth/value_depth use u32 while DataTypeMetadataInfo.max_depth is Option<u64>
description:
Completeness-critic finding: NOT voted by skeptics; verify before acting.

## metadata-server exceeds_max_depth/value_depth use u32 while DataTypeMetadataInfo.max_depth is Option<u64>
Crates: jmap-metadata-server (vs jmap-metadata-types)
Evidence: crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/capability.rs:74 `pub max_depth: Option<u64>`; crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/validate.rs:38 `pub fn value_depth(value: &Value) -> u32` and :68 `pub fn exceeds_max_depth(value: &Value, max_depth: u32) -> bool`. draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 line 262: `maxDepth: UnsignedInt|null`, and UnsignedInt goes up to 2^53-1. The sibling depth fields in the workspace are u64: graph-types search.rs:76,280 and filenode-server backend.rs:600.
Why breaking later: The intended call is `info.max_depth.map(|d| exceeds_max_depth(v, d as u32))`. An `as` cast wraps: a server or peer that advertises maxDepth 4294967296 becomes 0, so every write is rejected as too deep. A checked conversion has to pick a policy for the overflow case at each call site. Changing the parameter and return types to u64 later is a signature break on two public functions.
Fix: Before 0.4, change `value_depth` to return u64 and `exceeds_max_depth` to take `max_depth: u64`, or take `&DataTypeMetadataInfo` and handle the None case inside, so the types match the capability field and the workspace's other depth fields.
